title: The whole archive laid flat has no centre, so it perceives without a perceiver.
prompt:
No protagonist and no horizon. Two thousand small photographic fragments hang in a
pale field and drift at different speeds — a hand, a window, a strip of neon, a
shoulder. Nothing enters and nothing exits. Bands of density slowly migrate
upward like weather. Let fragments rhyme by shape rather than meaning: an ear
answers a doorway, a lamp answers an eye. Never let the camera settle long enough
for any fragment to become the subject. The film ends when the field has
redistributed itself, not when anything has happened.

title: Fourteen separate worlds become one world by being ruled into the same grid.
prompt:
Fourteen panels on one screen, all running at once, each a different poem's
weather: teal drowned room, orange stairwell, red heart on a chest, olive arch,
skeleton in bokeh, pale blue columns, neon and a red coat, rain on glass, blue
starburst, night road, two men on white ground, grey tunnel, a man in smoke, red
figure in lights. Never cut to a single panel. Instead let one element cross a
frame edge into its neighbour — a light leaves 07 and arrives in 08, a figure
walks out of 11 and into 12. The suite is proved by what can traverse it.

title: Sixteen nouns, each stacked into one picture, make meaning out of recurrence.
prompt:
Sixteen tiles, each a word becoming visible. Begin with all sixteen black. One at
a time, instances arrive and stack — 499 lights, 316 people, 248 windows, 10
doors — each arrival slightly brightening the tile and slightly shifting its
shape. Show the count rising in the corner. The film is over when every word has
been reached by enough examples to look like a thing. Where a word has too few
examples, leave it sparse and unresolved, and hold on it longest.

title: A room dissolved into its own atmosphere stops being a place and becomes a pressure.
prompt: A dim teal room that never resolves. Hold one fixed frame for four minutes. Furniture edges assemble and dissolve without ever agreeing. A window brightens somewhere left of centre and is gone. Vapour moves; nothing else does. No one enters. The room must feel inhabited by having been looked at too many times, not by anyone being in it.

title: One shot, sixteen pieces, and a white figure climbing out of an orange wall.
prompt: A burning orange stairwell, flat as a screenprint. One small white cut-out figure climbs. The stairwell is far too large for the figure and the colour far too loud for the event. Nothing else exists. As the figure climbs, the orange intensifies until it is the only fact in the frame. Keep the means visibly poor — hard edges, no gradient, no depth — so that scale does all the work.

poem: 03 HOW TO BREAK OFF AN ENGAGEMENT
title: A heart printed on a chest turns a body into the object that carries the story's force.
prompt: A man in red half-light, city bokeh behind him. Over his sternum a pale heart-shape sits like a decal, slightly wrong in scale, refusing to move with his breathing. Everything soft-focus except the heart, which stays hard-edged. Push in very slowly. Other people pass and none of them look at it. Do not explain it. End before anything happens to it.

title: A figure under an arch, seen past a bottle, at the hour when nothing is decided.
prompt: Olive-gold interior, one lamp burning above an arch. A seated figure, back to us, does not move. In the foreground a bottle stands far too large, in focus, present. Change almost nothing for two minutes. Once, the arch light dims and returns a half-second late. Once, the bottle's reflection shows a room that is not this one. Never cut away and never wake anybody.

title: A skeleton laid over a living body makes the past act on the present through the flesh.
prompt: A woman stands in red night light. Over her torso, an X-ray ribcage in the same red, breathing very slightly out of time with her. As she moves, the ribcage lags. Cut once to an older woman standing in exactly the same posture in a different decade, then back. The ribcage now keeps the older woman's time. Her next action must be caused by what the overlay showed.

title: A city built out of faces is a city that has to be read off the people who were in it.
prompt: A pale underwater plaza whose columns, on inspection, are made of standing human figures pressed into one another. Move slowly along the colonnade. Each column occasionally resolves into a face and loses it again. As the camera passes, new columns assemble behind from figures arriving. The city grows out of the bodies and the bodies are held up by the city. Never give a wide shot that settles the question.

title: Two men, one red coat, and a wall of neon slabs: the crowd as a single instrument.
prompt: A club street. Two men stand sharply separate in the foreground. Behind them the signage is not signage but a wall of vertical colour slabs that pulse together as one organism. A woman in red stands between the two conditions, her edges resolving and dissolving with the beat. Let the crowd's feeling arrive first in the slabs, then in her, and last in the two sharp men. No one leads.

title: Rain on glass turns a whole city into something that happens to a surface.
prompt: Fixed shot through a rain-covered window for six minutes. Beyond it a street exists only as smeared colour. Drops accumulate, merge, run, and clear a momentary lens through which something almost resolves and is lost. No one wipes the glass. No one arrives. Sound is only rain, glass, and distantly a city that will not be reached. Nothing in the frame can be responded to.

title: A burst of blue light behind two silhouettes turns an encounter into a shape.
prompt: Two people face each other against a hard blue radial burst that blows out every feature. Hold. Do not cut to what either of them sees, and never light their faces. The entire event is the minute change in the gap between the two silhouettes as the burst breathes. When the light finally drops enough to show a face, end the shot immediately.

title: A night road made of yellow lights is a journey with the journey taken out.
prompt: A night road with no car and no camera-in-a-car. Lamps recede in a yellow-green chain. Things pass through frame at the speed of a vehicle — a sign, a rail, a rectangle of light — but nothing is travelling. The road itself has the momentum. Hold until the absence of a traveller becomes the subject rather than an omission.

title: Two men walking on white ground: the world subtracted until only conduct is left.
prompt: White void, a colonnade in yellow light far behind. Two men walk the same line in opposite directions. Repeat the crossing many times with small variations: one hesitates, one shortens his stride, one carries something, one does not look. Never explain their relation. The meaning must accumulate only from the series of crossings, and vanish if the crossings are reordered.

title: A grey tunnel of mist is a place that has already had everything happen in it.
prompt: One continuous slow move down a misty street. At each depth a different decade is in progress: nearest figures present-day, mid-ground twenty years back, the far end further still. No dissolves, no flashback cues. Walking forward is going backward. Let a figure from one layer step into another and be unremarked. The street is the archive.

title: A man in blue smoke, assembled from three shots, is a portrait that will not settle.
prompt: A man in dark glasses in blue smoke. Film him as three overlapping performances of the same moment, offset by fractions of a second and a few degrees of posture. Never resolve them into one body. When he turns, the three turns do not arrive together. Do not use ghosting effects — shoot three real bodies occupying one intention. No name, no dialogue.

title: A red figure in bokeh: the everyday and the catastrophic at the same exposure.
prompt: A woman in a red coat stands at a crossing among ordinary city lights, waiting. She checks a phone. She shifts her weight. The light does not change. Keep the action entirely mundane and the colour entirely extreme. Somewhere off-frame something enormous is audible and never explained, and she does not react because she has heard it before. Give the burnt-out streetlamp as much attention as the sound.

title: Four hundred and ninety-nine lights on black become a constellation with no sky.
prompt: Pure black. Hundreds of small lights of every colour and shape drift at different rates — some flare, some are steady, some are the smeared trace of a light that moved during exposure. No lamp, no window, no street ever appears to explain any of them. Let them cluster into something that feels like a skyline, then let it disperse. The film is a city seen only as its emissions.

title: Three hundred and sixteen people stacked make a mass with no face and no edge.
prompt: A slow-moving mass of bodies, warm brown and mauve, so densely overlapped that no individual can be followed for more than a second. Occasionally one shoulder, one turn of a head, one hand becomes briefly distinct and is reabsorbed. The mass breathes as one. Never cut to a face. Feeling must travel across the whole body of it and never belong to anyone.

title: Two hundred and forty-eight windows agree on one thing: where the light gets in.
prompt: An interior assembled only from openings. Teal rectangles of daylight at incompatible scales hang in a dim room whose walls are never shown. Light moves across them as if from one sun, though they cannot share one. Nobody enters. Hold long enough that the room's expectancy becomes its own event.

title: Two hundred and twenty buildings stacked make one building that cannot be built.
prompt: A city that is only massing: grey-blue facades at every scale piled into one wall, with a strip of street-level activity along the bottom of frame. Follow one figure walking that strip. Every gesture — how far they keep from the wall, where they cross, what they look up at — should make the city's pressure more legible. Never show a whole building and never show the sky.

title: A hundred and seventy-six walls become a surface with weather on it.
prompt: A single wall filling the frame for its entire duration. Light crosses it, damp rises through it, paint lifts, a shadow of something unseen passes. At the bottom edge, small coloured things accumulate and are cleared away. Nothing is in front of the wall. The wall must acquire tension, expectancy and power without anyone arriving to give it any.

title: Ninety-nine faces over one another produce a face that belongs to no one and looks back.
prompt: A face slowly assembling from many faces. Begin with an unreadable blue-brown mass. Over four minutes let features arrive from different people — one person's eyes, another's mouth, another's jaw — never settling into a single face, always nearly one. At the right edge of frame, one whole woman's face remains sharp and unmerged throughout, watching. Do not cut to what she sees. End when the centre almost becomes her and does not.

title: Ninety-eight skies produce weather that no day ever had.
prompt: A sky that is all skies at once. A hot white core with pale blue radiating from it, crossed by orange streaks that behave like lens artefacts rather than light. Cloud forms assemble and are overrun by other cloud forms at a different scale. No horizon and no ground. Time of day changes continuously without ever passing through dusk. Nothing observes it.

title: Sixty-three hands, scattered and small, on a page that is mostly empty.
prompt: A pale empty field. Hands enter one at a time from nowhere, each already mid-gesture — gripping, pointing, reaching, cupping — hold, and leave. There is never anything to grip, point at, reach for, or hold. The gestures come faster. They begin to repeat. The film must make it clear that some force is moving these hands and that it is not intention.

title: Fifty-seven bodies in the air, on black, become one long red fall.
prompt: Darkness with a red-brown weight at its centre. Bodies in the air — falling, thrown, jumping, floating — arrive continuously from every direction and pass through one another without collision. There is no floor and no ceiling and no one lands. The same primitive force clearly governs all of it. Do not explain what the force is. Let a body occasionally slow almost to stillness before being taken again.

title: Fifty-six roads averaged into a horizontal smear: direction without destination.
prompt: A road seen from a fixed height, running left to right across frame. Nothing travels the whole length. Instead, separate journeys occupy separate stretches of it — a cyclist here, a truck there, someone walking a dog further along — none of them ever meeting. Slowly it becomes clear they are all on the same road at the same time. One pale structure stands at the centre and every journey passes it.

title: Forty-six lamps on black are objects that carry their own reason to be looked at.
prompt: Black. Forty-six lamps hang in the void, each lit, each lighting nothing but itself. Approach one — a small yellow shade. As you approach, the others dim. The room these lamps came from never appears. Something in the object is clearly held rather than emitted. Do not switch it off and do not reveal a hand.

title: Forty-six beds make a low teal mound: the place the whole archive keeps returning to.
prompt: A low teal mound in the dark, breathing very slightly, filmed as landscape rather than furniture. Hold on it. Over time, the impressions of bodies that have lain there rise and fade in the surface — not ghosts, just depressions that fill in slowly, as if the material had memory and was slow to forget. No one is in it. No one comes.

title: Forty-two signs from seven shots: language reduced to colour and left unread.
prompt: Black. Vertical strips of saturated neon colour, each obviously a word, none of them resolvable. Move past them as if along a street. Occasionally two strips align and almost form a phrase before separating. Show partial letters. Show a sign reflected in water where it is briefly more readable than the sign itself. Never let a full word be read. The viewer must assemble the street's language and fail.

title: Fifty-eight waters make a bright collision of surfaces that were never adjacent.
prompt: One continuous take through water in all its states. Begin on rain hitting a road; follow the runoff to a gutter; follow the gutter to a river; the river's surface becomes a reflection; the reflection becomes a window with rain on it; the rain becomes spray from a passing vehicle. Attention is handed on at each transfer and never returns. No character and no destination — only the passage of perceptual privilege through one substance.

title: Ten doors on a nearly empty page: too few to average, too many to ignore.
prompt: A pale empty room-sized field with a handful of doors standing in it, unattached to any wall. Someone opens the first: behind it, more of the same emptiness. They cross to the second and open it. Each opening reveals one more fact about a building that is not there — a draught, a sound, a change of floor. The situation is assembled entirely from what the doors imply and never shown.

title: Ten staircases: an orange flight, a dark frame, and the two never meet.
prompt: Two staircases in one space, at incompatible angles and scales — one hot orange and domestic, one dark and industrial. A figure climbs. Depending on which stair the camera favours, the same ascent reads as escape or as descent into a plant. Every new action supports both. Never establish which building this is, and never let the two stairs be seen to meet.

title: OUT OF LIFE as a place you could stand in, assembled from things that were never adjacent.
prompt: A place that was never photographed. A drowned teal bedroom that will not hold its edges. Hold it as a fixed frame with no one in it. Do not resolve the perspective and do not send anyone in. The location must acquire expectancy on its own, and the film ends before it is used for anything.

title: The same place in ink: the photograph and the dot field trade which one is real.
prompt: Two versions of one place, cut against each other: the photographic assemblage, and the same place in eight weights of black ink with a single blue. Then let something appear in the ink that has no counterpart in the photograph and stay there. End with the photograph looking like a memory of the dots.
